name: @prabhix/ui
description: Shared React UI primitives for Prabhix product webs.
//publishConfig: The exports above point at raw TypeScript, which is what a `file:` link wants: the app's
bundler follows the symlink and compiles the sources, so there is no build to run and no
dist to go stale while someone edits a primitive.
A published tarball cannot work that way -- Vite's Rollup build does not transpile
TypeScript inside node_modules, and Next needs the package in `transpilePackages` -- so npm
rewrites these three fields at pack time to serve the compiled output instead. Local
development keeps the link and the fast path; consumers installing by version get ordinary
ESM with declarations. Neither has to know about the other.
//files: src is kept alongside dist so the published sourcemaps resolve to real sources when a
consumer steps into a primitive in the debugger.
The tests are excluded. They import @testing-library, axe-core and vitest, which are dev
dependencies here and absent in every consumer, so shipping them puts unresolvable imports
in the tarball -- harmless while nothing reaches for them and a confusing failure the moment
something does, such as a consumer's own test runner globbing node_modules.
//: Everything this package imports is a peer, and every consuming app must declare all of them.
That is not a style choice. Apps link this package with `file:`, and npm does not install a
linked package's own dependencies into the consumer - it assumes the link target's tree will
serve. Vite's build agrees, because it resolves through the symlink to the real path. Vitest
does not: it inlines linked sources and resolves from the link path, inside the app's own
node_modules. So a dependency declared only here resolves at build time and fails at test
time, which is the worst way for it to fail.
Peers are therefore the only declaration that actually reaches the apps. The cost is that
adding a primitive means adding its package in every app too, and the cost of forgetting
used to be a red test suite in an unrelated file. `check-peers.mjs` in @prabhix/brand runs in
every repo's CI and fails with the exact npm command to run, so it is caught here instead.
react and react-dom are peers for the ordinary reason as well: hooks read a dispatcher off a
module-level singleton, and two copies fail as "Cannot read properties of null".
